name: Fluminense 2023 (Fernando Diniz)
scopeNote: Fluminense under Fernando Diniz, calendar year 2023 (Carioca won 9 Apr, Libertadores won 4 Nov v Boca 2-1 aet, Brasileirão 7th, Club World Cup final lost 0-4 to Manchester City 22 Dec). Period set by the user: 2023-01-14 (Resende 0-2 Fluminense) to 2023-12-22. Style term used by sources: 'Dinizismo' / 'jogo aposicional' (Diniz: 'anti-positional'; Blizzard also 'relationism'); the popular 'positional play' label is wrong, Diniz defines himself as the opposite of Guardiola's positional play. 2022 and 2024 material (Coaches' Voice piece is dated 2024-12 and mixes 2023-24 formations; Blizzard 2025, BTL 2024) is flagged retrospectiveOnly; 2024 facts (Colo-Colo, Mano Menezes, sacking) were dropped. Partial dates (YYYY or YYYY-MM) used where the day was not found. Marking (zonal vs man-oriented) has no in-period source naming a system, only Diniz's 'encaixar a marcacao' after the Club World Cup final, so axis mar is listed in gaps.axes and is answered from general knowledge.
openQuestions: Marking system (zonal vs man-oriented) was searched in Portuguese (marcação por zona / individual / homem a homem) and no in-period source answers it. Only indirect hints: Trivela final report cites a 'troca errada de marcação' by Marcelo (handover, suggests zone-oriented hand-offs); Diniz said in May 2024 (out of period) there are 'encaixes de marcação' that work sometimes. Left as gap.

Set-pieces: the '17 goals from set pieces, none conceded' (April 2023, Netvasco) was seen only in a search summary (unverified). Verified evidence is limited to taker hierarchy (Leo Fernández, Arias, Ganso) and Cano's chance from a Ganso set piece in the final.

Coaches' Voice five tactical keys (2024-12) lists 4-3-3/4-4-2/5-4-1 as main systems; 2023 sources (TFA, Blizzard) say 4-2-3-1 in possession and 4-4-2 out of possession (TSG). Shape in the CV piece was not used.

Defensive-block depth: TSG measures out-of-possession team length at 40 m and PPDA 7.33 (TFA), Coaches' Voice says high line; Trivela/TFA say Fluminense initially gave the opponent room at home in the final. Pressing height varied by match.
Diniz also became interim Brazil coach on 2023-07-04 (shared role until Jan 2024); effect on club rotation not evidenced.
People-management evidence is thin (training intensity, rest days, trust in John Kennedy); no direct dressing-room source for Marcelo/Keno integration in 2023.
Doentes por Futebol, Footure and Cartola Tática searches returned nothing readable; Trivela, The Athletic Brasil match analyses not found for the key games.

Gap-fill 2023-11-06 (marking): PT searches (marcação por zona/individual/encaixes; Mundial City) found no in-period tactical analysis of zonal vs man-oriented marking. Only Diniz's own post-City remark (2023-12) that the team 'conseguiu encaixar bem a marcação' (encaixe = man-oriented handoffs, unspecified) and Feb 2023 'volta pra compactar rápido'. Lance previews/Bragantino piece returned 404. Marking system stays unresolved; likely mixed/encaixe-based but not evidenced.

Gap-fill 2023-11-06 (pressing height): Diniz said in Feb 2023 'a tendência é marcar alto', 'pode ser que num momento a gente baixe' (primary, Carioca phase), consistent with the FIFA TSG high-pressing reading and Coaches' Voice high line; the home-final space given to Boca (TFA/Trivela) is therefore a match/game-state exception, not a season-long low block. No source found showing a phase-by-phase change in block depth.

sources.title: Cinco chaves táticas: Fernando Diniz no Fluminense - The Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: O estilo de jogo do Flu de Diniz pode ser identificado pela forma como a equipe inicia a saída de bola, sempre com três diretrizes: troca de passes, movimentação dos jogadores e a intenção de atrair os adversários.

sources.title: Cinco chaves táticas: Fernando Diniz no Fluminense - The Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: A característica mais significativa do Fluminense com a posse é o acúmulo de jogadores ao redor da bola.

sources.title: Cinco chaves táticas: Fernando Diniz no Fluminense - The Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Essa pressão começa desde o tiro de meta, com a ideia de impedir a progressão do rival. Se o adversário for corajoso e optar por jogar curto, os atacantes são os responsáveis por iniciar a pressão e tentar roubar a bola ou provocar uma saída longa. Essas bolas longas do adversário são protegidas por uma linha defensiva adiantada do Flu e pelo posicionamento dos meio-campistas para recuperar as segundas bolas

sources.title: Cinco chaves táticas: Fernando Diniz no Fluminense - The Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Isso é demonstrado por meio de um bloco compacto, que avança no terreno a cada bola dividida, bem como a cada passe para trás do adversário ou situação em que o adversário esteja de costas para a jogada

sources.title: Cinco chaves táticas: Fernando Diniz no Fluminense - The Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Ao ter mais jogadores que o adversário para fazer a pressão pós-perda, a equipe de Diniz consegue uma superioridade numérica na zona, o que exige um esforço menor de seus jogadores, com deslocamentos mais curtos para cortar linhas de passe e pressionar o portador da bola

sources.title: Sky Sports: The opposite of Pep - Fernando Diniz's innovative tactics with Fluminense
sources.evidence: "The way Pep likes having possession is the opposite of mine. His style is positional, mine is anti-positional."

sources.title: Sky Sports: The opposite of Pep - Fernando Diniz's innovative tactics with Fluminense
sources.evidence: "The full-backs come inside and play between the lines and this causes confusion for the opposition in terms of how they defend. It creates a dilemma for them. They do not know if they should press or stay to protect the zone because all the players are rotating.

sources.title: Sky Sports: The opposite of Pep - Fernando Diniz's innovative tactics with Fluminense
sources.evidence: "It is very particular. From the first phase of the build-up, he wants this very intensive rotation of his players. He tries to get the most technical players involved in that first phase to help the goalkeeper keep the ball and then progress up the field from there.

sources.title: Sky Sports: The opposite of Pep - Fernando Diniz's innovative tactics with Fluminense
sources.evidence: "The players react fast to put pressure on the ball. It is very aggressive and when he regains the ball, all the players are close together."

sources.title: Sky Sports: The opposite of Pep - Fernando Diniz's innovative tactics with Fluminense
sources.evidence: Imagine Jack Grealish drifting inside to play closer to Phil Foden. For Guardiola, this would just congest the space. Precisely what he does not want to happen. For Diniz, this would create an overload, increasing the likelihood of a give-and-go to unlock the defence.

sources.title: Sky Sports: The opposite of Pep - Fernando Diniz's innovative tactics with Fluminense
sources.evidence: "He graduated in psychology. He is very clever. He has a particular way of managing and motivating players. It is very interesting."

sources.title: FIFA Training Centre (TSG): Fluminense use possession game to book Club World Cup final berth
sources.evidence: An interesting feature of the Fluminense build-up was the lack of goalkeeper Fábio's (1) involvement – even when the team were building play from their own penalty area. Instead, and as demonstrated by clip 1 below, centre midfielder André (7) consistently dropped deep to assume a central role in his team's build-ups.

sources.title: FIFA Training Centre (TSG): Fluminense use possession game to book Club World Cup final berth
sources.evidence: A standout feature of Fluminense's in-possession game is their commitment to building play from the back. Even late in the game, when they were just 1-0 up in their semi-final, they remained fully committed to their build-up style.

sources.title: FIFA Training Centre (TSG): Fluminense use possession game to book Club World Cup final berth

sources.title: FIFA Training Centre (TSG): Fluminense use possession game to book Club World Cup final berth

sources.title: FIFA Training Centre (TSG): Fluminense use possession game to book Club World Cup final berth

sources.title: FIFA Training Centre (TSG): Fluminense use possession game to book Club World Cup final berth
